extracted.subtask_description: Newspaper-page collection of wartime dispatches, military communiqués, political reports, and civil-policy notices intended to inform the general public about ongoing war events and related domestic measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Night fighter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A night fighter must be put into action at once; it must be armed heavily enough to bring down big German bombers and have fuel capacity to stay aloft for the duration of at least one series of attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains operational and design requirements: heavy armament to defeat four‑engined Dorniers and Junkers, sufficient fuel endurance to remain on station through an attack series, and immediate deployment rather than distant-future delivery. Also notes practical difficulties of night interception (visibility limited to exhaust glow or silhouette against searchlights) and that experiments with other defensive devices are ongoing but no successful night fighter yet exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air defense composition: fighters plus anti-aircraft
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-aircraft guns alone are insufficient as the sole defense; fighters are essential to clear enemy bombers from the night skies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument in the article: AA barrages may comfort shelter-bound civilians but have proven inadequate to stop repeated nightly raids. A successful defense requires fighters capable of night interception; experimental devices exist but are unproven, so emphasis is on producing effective night fighters immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting censorship on London damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the British now forbid any mention of specific damage in London, outside observers will not be told precise damage until after the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a reporting restriction imposed by British authorities; journalists are to avoid publishing specific damage details, so public reports will be intentionally vague or withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Legion resolution on hyphenated American names
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution declaring that 'hyphenated American name shall be deemed subversive to American principles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Legion ordered its legislative committee to seek suitable legislation 'outlawing the same.' This is a stated organizational policy and proposed legal/political standard coming out of the American Legion convention coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Japanese-Indo-China agreement terms (limited military facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreements with Japan contained formal Japanese guaranties to respect Indo-China's territorial integrity and French sovereignty and precisely limited the military facilities granted to Japan; the French agreed to permit Japanese to enter only by the port of Haiphong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article reports French insistence that Japan violated the accord by moving troops into northern Indo-China. The phrasing captures diplomatic/contractual standards: guarantees of territorial integrity, sovereignty, and strict geographic/port limits on military entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submarine effectiveness metric: tonnage sunk
rubrics_metrics.description: Success of submarine commanders is measured and reported by the tonnage of enemy merchant shipping sunk (e.g., 'has sunk 151,400 tons of enemy merchant shipping').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a public metric and ranking for submarine commanders in official communiqués and news reporting; tonnage-sunk figures are cited as accomplishments and to top lists of commanders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian resource-conservation rule: restricted bicycle use for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministry of Education decree: children who still own bicycles may not use them except to ride to and from school; visits to friends or rural excursions are deemed a waste of rubber tires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violators will be punished by confiscation of the tires. This is a domestic wartime conservation regulation governing civilian behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian passive defense guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Population urged to support a passive defense by remaining calm; schools closed in certain areas as a precautionary measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as part of colonial/local civil-defense measures (e.g., in Indo-China) to reduce panic and maintain order during military operations; procedural guidance rather than evaluative commentary.
